title: Measurable Hilbert Fields and Direct-Integral Operators

items.title: Von Neumann algebras and commutants
items.statement: Assume AC. On a complex Hilbert space H, a concrete von Neumann algebra is a unital star-subalgebra of B(H) closed in the weak operator topology. For S⊂B(H), S' is its commutant, S'' its double commutant, and W*(S) the weak-operator closure of the unital star-algebra generated by S. Commutants are taken inside B(H); no bicommutant theorem is built into these definitions.
items.strategy: Check that S' is a unital star-algebra when S is self-adjoint, and is weak-operator closed because each equation TS=ST is closed under matrix-coefficient limits. These observations license later use of commutants; do not assert W*(S)=S'' without a proof.
items.axiom_use: Applying def-axiom-of-choice to a family indexed by the natural numbers supplies Countable Choice, the hypothesis of thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties, which supplies adjoints on B(H) and its involution. No further choice is used.

references.title: C. Anantharaman and S. Popa, An Introduction to II1 Factors
F. Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Ch. 10

items.title: Measurable Hilbert field from a countable fundamental family
items.statement: Let (X,S,μ) be a sigma-finite standard-Borel measure space. A measurable complex Hilbert field consists of separable fibres H_x and a specified sequence e_n(x) with measurable Gram coefficients x↦<e_n(x),e_m(x)> and fibrewise dense complex-linear span. A section ξ is measurable when x↦<ξ(x),e_n(x)> is measurable for every n. Zero fibres and noncomplete measures are allowed; equivalence is only μ-almost everywhere.
items.strategy: Verify the Gram condition makes every e_n measurable and gives a countable field of rational linear combinations that is dense in every fibre. Specify the inner-product convention as linear in the first variable, matching the existing Hilbert-space page. No measurability of an arbitrary raw field or completeness of μ is presumed.

references.title: B. Bekka and P. de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters
F. Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Ch. 10

items.title: Measurable sections have measurable pointwise inner products
items.statement: For the preceding countable measurable Hilbert field, the fundamental-family coefficient criterion is equivalent to testing against every measurable section. The norm of each measurable section and the pointwise inner product of any two measurable sections are measurable. Measurable sections are closed under measurable scalar combinations and pointwise norm limits.
items.strategy: Explicitly enumerate finite rational-complex combinations by coding each (fundamental index, rational real part, rational imaginary part) with the natural-pairing bijection, then coding the finite list as a natural number; malformed codes decode to the empty sum. Rational density gives density in each fibre, and one fixed rational/natural bijection plus explicit coding avoids countable choice. Prove each q_j coefficient and norm measurable from finite Gram expansions and Borel scalar maps. Use the countable normalized pairings to recover ||ξ||, including zero fibres. For each k, partition by the least j with ||η-q_j||<1/k; the resulting measurable q_{j_k} approximates η. Pointwise limits and Cauchy–Schwarz give the all-section pairing direction, and testing against e_n gives the reverse direction. State the exact complex coordinate basis, Borel-composition, and modulus suppliers used in these steps.

references.title: B. Bekka and P. de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters
F. Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Ch. 10

items.title: A separably acting abelian von Neumann algebra has a self-adjoint generator
items.statement: Assume AC. If H is a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space and A⊂B(H) is an abelian von Neumann algebra, there is a bounded self-adjoint S∈A with A=W*(S).
items.strategy: Derive a dense sequence from the definition of separability (the nonzero hypothesis rules out an empty dense subset). Riesz representation turns WOT tests into matrix coefficients. On the operator unit ball, the coefficients on that sequence induce WOT: approximation on the unit ball controls coefficients for arbitrary vectors. Since C is second countable and N×N is countable, the coefficient map into C^(N×N) gives a countable base; restriction gives one for A's unit ball, and AC selects one element from each nonempty basic open set. The countable-product and Riesz suppliers consume only ACω, supplied by AC. Take the self-adjoint real and imaginary parts. For each, dyadic-threshold spectral projections belong to A: continuous calculus puts bounded continuous approximants in the norm-closed algebra A, and the published bounded Borel calculus gives their strong limits. Enumerate this family by an explicit pairing of its four natural indices; its projections commute, and dyadic spectral step functions norm-approximate each chosen self-adjoint operator. Form S=Σ_j 3^{-j}P_j in norm. For the k-th digit, the finitely many length-k cylinder intervals [s_k,s_k+3^{-k}/2] are pairwise disjoint with a positive gap; define a continuous piecewise-linear real function that is 0 on the intervals whose k-th digit is 0 and 1 on those whose k-th digit is 1. Every finite ternary sum with at least k digits lies in its corresponding cylinder, so finite joint spectral projections give f_k(S_N)=P_k for N≥k. Prove f_k(S_N)→f_k(S) by polynomial approximation on the common compact interval, so every P_k∈W*(S). Their WOT-closed generated algebra contains the selected WOT-dense unit ball and hence equals A.

references.title: C. Anantharaman and S. Popa, An Introduction to II1 Factors
B. Bekka and P. de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters

items.axiom_use: AC supplies its ACω consequence required by the Riesz-representation and countable-product suppliers, and selects one operator from each nonempty member of a countable WOT base restricted to A's unit ball. It also supplies the explicit AC hypotheses of the adjoint and functional-calculus suppliers. The dyadic threshold projections and their enumeration are explicit, with no additional choices.

items.title: Direct integral of a measurable Hilbert field
items.statement: The direct integral ∫_X^⊕ H_x dμ(x) is the quotient of measurable sections ξ with ∫||ξ(x)||²dμ<∞ by μ-almost-everywhere equality, with <[ξ],[η]>=∫<ξ(x),η(x)>dμ(x). This is a well-defined inner-product space; the Hilbert completion is proved in the next theorem.
items.strategy: Use the preceding field and section results for measurability of ||ξ||² and <ξ,η>, and Borel composition for squaring norms and taking complex moduli. Declare the real/complex inner-product, scalar L² and L¹ quotient, Cauchy–Schwarz, integral, and conjugation/modulus suppliers directly. Prove square-integrable sections are closed under sums by ||ξ+η||²≤2(||ξ||²+||η||²); use monotonicity, positive homogeneity, and additivity of the nonnegative integral to infer finiteness. Prove closure under scalar multiplication directly. Use finite unions of Borel null sets to show a.e. equality is an equivalence relation and the operations respect classes. Fibrewise Cauchy–Schwarz followed by scalar L² Cauchy–Schwarz and monotonicity of the integral makes <ξ,η> integrable. Prove representative independence by the a.e.-invariance theorem for the integral, linearity by the L¹ integral theorem, and positive definiteness by the nonnegative-zero-integral theorem. Retain the noncompletion convention and claim only an inner-product space; completeness is the next theorem.

references.title: B. Bekka and P. de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters
references.locator: Ch. 1 §1.G, printed pp. 59–60 (fundamental family, measurable sections, almost-everywhere classes, and direct-integral inner product)

references.title: F. Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Ch. 10
references.locator: Part III, Ch. 10 §§1.3–1.4, printed pp. 94–96 (L² quotient and deferred Riesz–Fischer completeness on p. 95; measurable-field criterion and square-integrability criterion on p. 96)

items.title: Direct integrals of measurable Hilbert fields are Hilbert spaces
items.statement: Assume AC. For a sigma-finite standard-Borel base and a measurable Hilbert field with countable fundamental family, the direct integral is complete. It is separable. The countable-choice cost of selecting representatives and the AC-qualified standard-Borel suppliers are part of the claim.
items.strategy: For a Cauchy sequence choose least-index subsequence with successive L² distances below 2^{-k}; AC chooses its countably many measurable representatives. Minkowski plus monotone convergence makes g=Σ_k||ξ_{k+1}-ξ_k|| finite a.e. and in L². Outside the measurable null set the vector series converges in each complete H_x; set the limit to zero on that set. Coefficient tests are pointwise limits, hence the new section is measurable; the tail bound by g and dominated convergence yield L² convergence, then the full Cauchy sequence converges. For separability, use the published bimeasurable real coding and countable determining algebra to fix a countable generating algebra, adjoin one finite-measure exhaustion, and prove by a finite-measure pi-lambda/monotone-class argument that its rational simple functions are dense in scalar L². Fibrewise Gram–Schmidt on the fundamental sequence gives measurable orthonormal sections with zero vectors on dependent fibres. Parseval plus dominated convergence approximates any section by finite coordinate truncations; approximate each scalar L² coefficient by the countable rational simple family. Thus finite rational combinations of these frame sections and algebra indicators form a countable dense set.

references.title: B. Bekka and P. de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters
F. Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Ch. 10
C. Anantharaman and S. Popa, An Introduction to II1 Factors

items.axiom_use: AC selects countably many measurable representatives and supplies the coding/determining-algebra and Parseval supplier hypotheses.

items.title: Measurable and decomposable operator fields
items.statement: For a measurable field (H_x,e_n), an operator field x↦T_x∈B(H_x) is weakly measurable if every x↦<T_x e_n(x),e_m(x)> is measurable; equivalently it is weakly measurable against all measurable sections once the boundedness condition is imposed. It is essentially bounded if ess sup_x||T_x||<∞. A bounded operator T on the direct integral is decomposable if T[ξ]=[x↦T_xξ(x)] for such a field, with equality of fields understood almost everywhere.
items.strategy: Explicitly encode every rational-complex finite combination using the finite-sequence code, one rational/natural bijection and the published natural-pair pairing; prove density from the dense fundamental span and rational density, using the fibre norm axioms. Normalize the tests by a measurable reciprocal-norm scalar with zero sent to zero. Expand matrix coefficients to prove each T_x q_j measurable, and prove ||T_x|| = sup_{j,k}|<T_x u_j,u_k>| using the dense normalized family, Cauchy–Schwarz and continuity; encode pairs by N×N≈N and apply countable-supremum measurability. Prove the coefficient-test/all-measurable-section equivalence locally by least-index approximation and pointwise limits, which need only pointwise boundedness of each T_x. Define decomposable operators with explicit square-integrable action membership; the next theorem proves every essentially bounded measurable field has that action. Equality of fields is modulo a measurable null set. The coding and least-index arguments use no AC.

references.title: B. Bekka and P. de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters
F. Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Ch. 10

items.axiom_use: No axiom of choice is used: the countable rational family is inherited from the explicit coding in the section lemma, and section approximations use least natural indices.

items.title: Measurable essentially bounded operator fields act decomposably
items.statement: Assume AC. Every weakly measurable essentially bounded field (T_x) induces a well-defined bounded operator T=∫^⊕T_x with ||T||=ess sup_x||T_x||. The fields (T_x*) and (T_xS_x) are weakly measurable and essentially bounded whenever the inputs are, and the induced adjoint and product are T* and TS.
items.strategy: From measurable matrix coefficients and the measurable norm, choose for each k the least rational fundamental combination within 1/k of an arbitrary measurable section; after localization to sets where ||T_x||≤M, this proves T_xξ(x) measurable by pointwise limits. The bound ||T_xξ||≤M||ξ|| proves square integrability and representative independence; fibrewise adjoint coefficients are conjugates and products are measurable by the same approximation. For the reverse norm bound, normalize the countable rational span fields to norm ≤1. The pointwise operator norm is their supremum; if M<ess sup||T_x||, one candidate exceeds M on a positive-measure set. Intersect with a finite-measure exhaustion set and localize that candidate to get a nonzero direct-integral vector with ||Tξ||>M||ξ||. This also handles zero fibres.

references.title: B. Bekka and P. de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters
F. Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Ch. 10

items.axiom_use: AC propagates the Hilbert-space completeness assumption from the direct-integral theorem; no stronger choice is used in the operator norm argument.

items.title: Decomposable operators are the commutant of diagonal multiplication
items.statement: Assume AC. For a sigma-finite standard-Borel measurable Hilbert field with countable fundamental family, let D={M_f:f∈L∞(X,μ)} act on its direct integral by scalar multiplication. Then D' is exactly the algebra of decomposable bounded operators. Each decomposable field is unique up to μ-null sets on nonzero fibres.
items.strategy: The scalar field f(x)I is weakly measurable and essentially bounded, so the action theorem defines M_f independently of its representative; pointwise field action gives the decomposable-operator inclusion. Conversely choose an increasing Borel exhaustion by finite-measure sets and the bounded normalized countable family obtained from rational finite combinations of the fundamental sections. AC chooses representatives of the countably many localized images S(1_{E_k}u_n). Commutation makes these representatives agree almost everywhere on overlaps; glue them after removing one Borel null set. For each rational-complex finite combination and each measurable subset of E_k, the operator-norm bound gives an integral inequality; threshold sets and the nonnegative-integral rules turn it into one pointwise bound outside a common conull set. Extend the resulting rational-linear assignment continuously to each fibre, set it to zero on exceptional and zero fibres, and verify weak measurability by the fundamental coefficient criterion. The action theorem identifies its induced operator with S on the dense span of bounded scalar localizations of the normalized sections; prove that density by least-index measurable selection and finite truncation. The same localized sections prove almost-everywhere uniqueness. Check the empty space, zero and one-dimensional fibres, varying finite dimensions, null sets, and both commutant inclusions.

references.title: F. Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Ch. 10
references.locator: Part III, Chapter 10 §1.8, Theorem 2, printed pp. 100–101; the local proof adapts its commutant reconstruction to the standard-Borel field convention.

references.title: B. Bekka and P. de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters
references.locator: Chapter 1 §1.H, Theorems 1.H.1 and 1.H.4, printed pp. 65–68; general-field statement and detailed constant-separable-fibre proof.

items.axiom_use: Assume AC to meet the hypotheses of the commutant, direct-integral Hilbert-space, and operator-action suppliers. AC also supplies a countable choice of measurable representatives for S(1_{E_k}u_n). The normalized test family, finite rational coding, least-index measurable partitions, finite-measure exhaustion, and fibre extensions are otherwise explicit; no further choice is used.

items.title: Diagonal multipliers form a von Neumann algebra
items.statement: Assume AC. In the preceding direct integral, the diagonal multiplication algebra D={M_f:f∈L∞(X,μ)} is a concrete abelian von Neumann algebra and satisfies D''=D, even when zero fibres make f↦M_f nonfaithful.
items.strategy: First prove D is a unital abelian *-subalgebra. The commutant theorem gives D'=all decomposable operators. For T∈D'', D⊂D' implies T∈D', so write T=∫T_x. Normalize the countable fundamental sections and construct bounded weakly measurable rank-one fields R_{n,m}(x):ξ↦<ξ,u_n(x)>u_m(x). Their induced operators lie in D', so T commutes with them. Product compatibility and a.e. uniqueness of fields give fibrewise commutation outside a common Borel null set. The diagonal rank-one projections make each nonzero fundamental direction an eigenvector; the off-diagonal rank-one maps show all eigenvalues agree. Density then gives T_x=λ(x)I, including zero fibres. Recover λ measurably on the least-index partition by the first nonzero normalized section, set it to zero on zero fibres and the exceptional null set, and use essential boundedness of T_x. Thus T=M_λ and D''=D; commutants are WOT closed.

references.title: F. Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Ch. 10
references.locator: Part III, Chapter 10 §1.8, Theorem 3, printed pp. 101–102 (continuous/Lusin field convention)

references.title: B. Bekka and P. de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters
references.locator: Chapter 1 §1.H, Proposition 1.H.2, printed pp. 65–66 (constant-field diagonal multipliers)

items.axiom_use: Assume AC to meet the hypotheses of the direct-integral action theorem, the decomposable-commutant theorem, and the von Neumann algebra/adjoint conventions. The normalized fundamental family, countable exceptional-set union, and least-index scalar partition are explicit and use no additional choice.

items.title: Spectral multiplicity model for separably acting abelian von Neumann algebras
items.statement: Assume AC. Let A⊂B(H) be an abelian von Neumann algebra on a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space. There are a bounded self-adjoint generator S∈A, a nonzero finite regular Borel measure μ on compact K=σ(S)⊂R, a Borel multiplicity m:K→{1,2,...}∪{∞} defined μ-a.e., and a unitary U:H→∫_K^⊕ C^{m(t)}dμ(t) such that USU⁻¹=M_t and UAU⁻¹={M_f:f∈L∞(K,μ)}. For a fixed generator S, the measure class and multiplicity are unique up to almost-everywhere equality on K; changing S may change the parameter coordinate.
items.strategy: Choose the bounded self-adjoint generator and decompose into cyclic spectral measures. Construct a common finite regular measure from their positive weighted sum, then use Radon–Nikodym densities, active sets, and an explicit Borel active-rank map to build the varying-dimensional field and unitary locally; justify the density-integral identity from the RN set formula using simple functions and monotone convergence. For the algebra identity, use WOT closedness for one inclusion. For the reverse inclusion, approximate the real and imaginary parts of each bounded Borel multiplier separately by real-valued C(K) functions in a finite regular measure weighted by a countable dense vector sequence, clip the approximants radially, and prove SOT convergence first on that sequence and then on all vectors from the uniform bound. For fixed-generator uniqueness, use a weighted spectral scalar measure to identify the common measure class, transfer equivalent measures by the RN square-root unitary, and put the intertwiner in an off-diagonal block over the direct-sum field. Apply the local varying-field commutant and fibrewise product/adjoint clauses to obtain fibre unitaries on one common conull set, forcing the multiplicities to agree. Do not rely on the published independence lemma.

references.title: C. Anantharaman and S. Popa, An Introduction to II1 Factors
F. Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Ch. 10
B. Bekka and P. de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters

items.axiom_use: Assume AC. It supplies the hypotheses of the self-adjoint-generator and countable cyclic-decomposition results, the RN theorem, and the direct-integral Hilbert-space, operator-field, and commutant results. AC also gives DC and countable choice for the regularity and real C_c-density suppliers, and the standard-Borel presentation of the Borel subset K of R. It permits countable dense representatives and cyclic choices. The weighted sums, active-rank enumeration, clipping map, and local RN integral identity are explicit.

title: Measurable Hilbert Fields and Direct-Integral Operators: Examples

items.title: Direct integral of a constant Hilbert field
items.statement: Assume AC. For a sigma-finite standard-Borel (X,μ) and a separable complex Hilbert space K with a fixed finite or countable orthonormal basis, the constant field H_x=K has direct integral naturally isometric to L²(X,μ;K), the space of K-valued maps whose basis coefficients are Borel measurable and whose squared norms are integrable, modulo almost-everywhere equality. Its coordinate map identifies it with the Hilbert sum of scalar complex L²(X,μ) spaces. For counting measure on a countable X this is the ordinary Hilbert sum ⊕_{x∈X}K.
items.strategy: Take constant sections from the chosen orthonormal basis, padding a finite or empty basis by zero sections to meet the countable-fundamental-family convention. Weak coordinate measurability equals section measurability for a separable constant fibre. Parseval and monotone convergence give the coordinate norm identity; nonnegative-integral additivity makes finite-coordinate sections square-integrable. The coordinate map is an isometry whose image contains every finitely supported tuple. The direct-integral completeness theorem lets limits of truncations realize every square-summable coordinate tuple. Under counting measure the integral norm is Σ_x||ξ(x)||². Check the empty base, zero and one-dimensional fibres, finite bases, null sets, and the exact AC use.

references.title: B. Bekka and P. de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters
F. Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Ch. 10
references.locator: Part III, Chapter 10 §§1.3–1.5, printed pp. 95–96; continuous-field construction and fibrewise orthogonalization

items.axiom_use: Assume AC. It supplies the direct-integral completeness result and the Countable Choice hypothesis of the Parseval theorem. The basis is fixed in the example, and the finite-coordinate construction and limit are canonical; no additional choice is used.

items.title: Multiplicity-two diagonal representation
items.statement: Assume AC. Let λ be Borel Lebesgue measure on [0,1], H=L²([0,1],λ;C²), S=M_t⊗I₂, and D={M_f⊗I₂:f∈L∞([0,1],λ)}. Then D is an abelian concrete von Neumann algebra with D=W*(S), the fixed-generator spectral multiplicity is m(t)=2 almost everywhere, and D′ consists exactly of essentially bounded Borel measurable 2-by-2 matrix fields modulo almost-everywhere equality; D′ is nonabelian.
items.strategy: Identify the constant field with L²(λ)⊕L²(λ). Compute σ(S)=[0,1] directly using bounded reciprocal multipliers off the interval and normalized small-interval indicators on it. Construct the regular indicator-multiplication PVM, verify its coordinate integral is S, and identify it by the A-side spectral theorem's uniqueness clause. Prove D=W*(S) by bounded continuous approximation and strong convergence. Compute both cyclic measures and an explicit weighted multiplicity-two model. Use the local commutant and operator-action theorems to identify the four measurable matrix entries, then exhibit noncommuting matrix units.

references.title: C. Anantharaman and S. Popa, An Introduction to II1 Factors
B. Bekka and P. de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters

items.axiom_use: Assume AC for the direct-integral Hilbert-space, fixed-generator multiplicity, commutant, and operator-action results. AC implies DC and Countable Choice for the cited continuous-density, Lebesgue-measure, regularity, and adjoint suppliers. The cyclic vectors, their scalar measures, the weights and RN densities, and the matrix units are explicit; no further choice is used.

items.title: A measurable two-dimensional operator field
items.statement: Assume AC. On the preceding multiplicity-two field over [0,1], the matrix field T_t=[[0,t],[1-t,0]] is weakly measurable and essentially bounded. Its induced operator has norm 1, adjoint field [[0,1-t],[t,0]], and square field t(1-t)I₂. It commutes with every diagonal multiplier but is not itself in the diagonal algebra.
items.strategy: Check the four Borel matrix coefficients and compute ||T_t||=max(t,1-t); positive-measure intervals near the endpoints prove the essential supremum is 1. Apply the action theorem for the operator norm, adjoint and square, verify pointwise commutation with scalar matrices, and use the image of the first constant basis vector to separate the induced operator from every diagonal multiplier.

references.title: B. Bekka and P. de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters
F. Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups, Ch. 10

items.axiom_use: Assume AC for the measurable-field action theorem. AC implies DC and Countable Choice, supplying the countable-choice hypothesis of the Lebesgue box theorem used for positive-measure endpoint neighborhoods. All matrix entries, norm calculations, and the vector witness are explicit; no further choice is used.
